notes.note: Gen 26 has no absolute date for the famine and Isaac's sojourn at Gerar. I anchor the famine loosely after the birthright sale (25:29-34, Isaac c. 79) and Abraham's death with MACRO_ERA and a wide margin. Esau's marriage at 40 (26:34) is dated exactly from the twins' birth; it falls in the same broad period and its order relative to the Gerar scenes is not given by the text, so it carries no causal link to them.

Divine speeches in this chapter: 26:2-5 (stay in the land, blessing, oath to Abraham) and 26:24 (fear not, I will bless you and multiply your seed). The multiplication of Isaac's seed is fulfilled in later chapters (Jacob's family); the session for those chapters writes that link. Every verse of the chapter 1-35 is covered by an event; none left out.

Gen 26 has no absolute date for the famine and Isaac's sojourn at Gerar. I anchor the famine loosely after the birthright sale (25:29-34, Isaac c. 79) and Abraham's death with MACRO_ERA and a wide margin. Esau's marriage at 40 (26:34) is dated exactly from the twins' birth; it falls in the same broad period and its order relative to the Gerar scenes is not given by the text, so it carries no causal link to them.

Divine speeches in this chapter: 26:2-5 (stay in the land, blessing, oath to Abraham) and 26:24 (fear not, I will bless you and multiply your seed). The multiplication of Isaac's seed is fulfilled in later chapters (Jacob's family); the session for those chapters writes that link. Every verse of the chapter 1-35 is covered by an event; none left out.

[event:evt.gen_26.famine_to_gerar] Rashi/Sforno-type tradition places this famine after Abraham's death; the packet's Sforno comment only says it was severe. I chose a 5-year offset from the birthright sale with a 15-year margin. Isaac's starting point is taken as the Negev/Beer-lahai-roi area (25:11) and Gerar is about 34 km by road from Beersheba, so I allow 2 days of travel.

[event:evt.gen_26.theophany_stay] Placed after the arrival in Gerar (26:1), although a reading (Pseudo-Jonathan: Isaac had in mind to go down to Egypt) could put it on the road before Gerar. Order within a few weeks only.

[event:evt.gen_26.abimelech_window] 'When the days were long' is unquantified; 1 year offset, 1 year margin. Abimelech here is probably not the Abimelech of Gen 20 in the same person (the packet ids him as person.abimelech.gen_20_2); not decided here, left to the ontologist.

[event:evt.gen_26.prosperity_envy] Verse 15 (wells stopped by the Philistines) is background pluperfect, after Abraham's death, and is placed with the envy it explains. Duration 2 years is a guess for 'went on growing'; it is not stated.

[event:evt.gen_26.wells_esek] The sequence Esek, Sitnah, Rehoboth takes unstated weeks to months; the offsets are estimates and the tier is MACRO_ERA. The reopening of Abraham's wells (v18) and the digging in the wadi (v19) are taken as one phase. The Targum Pseudo-Jonathan version of v20 (the well dried up and then flowed again for Isaac) is not used.

[event:evt.gen_26.move_to_beersheba] Rehoboth to Beersheba is about 44 km by road, about 1 day by donkey with herds (urim travel); with a household and flocks I allow 2 days. Rehoboth/Sitnah share coordinates in the registry (identification uncertain, 0.3-0.56), so the figure is approximate.

[event:evt.gen_26.abimelech_covenant] Gerar to Beersheba is about 34 km by road (1 day by donkey); the delegation arrives some days or weeks after the altar and the digging of the well, offset 2 weeks with a 2-week margin. The feast (v30) is the same evening; the oath is the next morning (v31, BOKER, counted midnight to midnight).

[event:evt.gen_26.esau_marries] Isaac was 60 at the twins' birth (25:26), so Esau 40 is Isaac 100; compare anchor.isaac_birth + 100 years: the same date, as anchored on the birth event. Anchored on the birth event for the age. Esau's marriage is the one date in the chapter that fixes the period (c. 1967 BCE on the packet's numbers), which falls about 20 years after the birthright sale; so the Gerar sojourn probably lies near it. Verse 35 (the wives' bitterness) is included in the same event.

[causal:caus.gen_26.theophany_stay.gerar_dwelling] The command to stay is followed by Isaac dwelling in Gerar (26:6); I treat the obedience as TRIGGERS, not a prophecy fulfilment, since 26:2 is a command, not a prediction.

[causal:caus.gen_26.theophany_stay.sowing_blessed] 26:3 'I will be with you and bless you' is read as fulfilled at 26:12 'the LORD blessed him' and the hundredfold; confidence below 1 because the text does not tie the two.
[entity:group.hittites] Heth@Gen.10.15 not defined as a person: 'the Hittite' here is a gentilic, so the existing group.hittites is used (MENTIONED in esau_marries).

[entity:person.abimelech.gen_20_2] Registry id kept from Gen 20; the corpus has no Gen 20 yet, so he is defined here. Whether this king is the Abimelech of Abraham's day or a dynastic title is left open.
[entity:person.adah] Registry gives Adah for the 'Basemath' of 26:34 (Gen 36 harmonisation). Id kept from the registry; canonical name is the text's Basemath, Adah is an alias.
[entity:group.hittites] Heth@Gen.10.15 not defined as a person: 'the Hittite' here is a gentilic, so the existing group.hittites is used (MENTIONED in esau_marries).
[entity:loc.philistia] Defined for the registry tag; the Philistines as people are a separate group.philistines without a tipnr_id.
[event_links:evt.gen_26.theophany_stay] Place Gerar carried over from the previous scene; the text does not name where Isaac is when the LORD appears.
[event_links:evt.gen_26.esau_marries] No place given in the text, so left out. Isaac and Rebekah are PATIENTs as those who feel the grief.
[event_links:evt.gen_26.abimelech_covenant] Place is Beersheba (carried over): Abimelech comes to Isaac there from Gerar (26:26).

[component:comp.isaac.dwelling.2] Chain of dwellings is inferred from the verbs 'dwelt' (26:6, 26:17) and 'went up' (26:23); the opening of Gerar as a dwelling is dated to 26:6, although he arrives at 26:1.
[component:comp.isaac.fear.1] Inferred state: the text gives fear at 26:7; its end at 26:11 is my reading of Abimelech's protection.
[component:comp.philistines.attitude.1] Closing at 26:28 is inferred from the delegation's change of tone; Isaac's own 'you hate me' (26:27) is the other side.
[system:sys.royal_edict_of_protection] New system defined here; no existing system fit a royal decree of protection.
[system:sys.covenant_feast] New system defined here for the meal that precedes the oath.

[event_links:evt.gen_26.well_sitnah] 'They dug' in 26:21 is ambiguous: servants of Isaac assumed; quarrellers assumed the herdsmen of Gerar. Place is Sitnah; wadi of Gerar is the setting but Sitnah is used as the named well.
